newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle market inactive - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle market inactive - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets near midday Monday were inactive, with no reported trades, feedlot sources said.
A few bids at $65.00 to $66.00 per cwt were passed by owners asking $68.00 to $69.00, they said.
The bulk of last week's cattle sold at $68.00, although there were a few sales at $67.00 Thursday and Friday.

Some cattle feeders said they expect cattle to sell this week at $67.00, with support from hefty beef sales last week offset by a recent weakening of beef prices and perceptions that showlists are larger this week than last, sources said.

Some cattle on this week's Texas Panhandle showlists were expected to be relatively light weight following snow, cold and heavy rain late last week, which stressed animals, sources there said. But concern over reduced weight gains of cattle in Texas should be short-lived, they said.
Muddy feedlots after the storms were also stressing cattle but conditions were seen improving early this week amid expected temperatures in the 70s (Fahrenheit), sources said.
Cattle in Kansas and western Oklahoma were largely unaffected as the storm was mostly concentrated in Texas and southern Oklahoma.
